dayDefinition.stage4: 24 hours ending 1200 UTC on the date

stage4.provider: NOAA National Weather Service (NWS), National Centers for Environmental Prediction (NCEP); mosaic of River Forecast Center analyses
stage4.dataset: Stage IV daily multisensor (radar and rain gauge) quantitative precipitation estimate, 24-hour totals ending 1200 UTC
stage4.nativeGrid: HRAP polar stereographic, 1121 x 881 cells, about 3.8 km at 30 N
stage4.units: inches in the source; converted here with 1 inch = 25.4 mm

atlas14.provider: NOAA National Weather Service, Hydrometeorological Design Studies Center (HDSC)
atlas14.dataset: NOAA Atlas 14 point precipitation frequency estimates, partial duration series, with 90% confidence bounds

nasa.provider: NASA Langley Research Center, POWER project
nasa.dataset: POWER daily point data at source native resolution: IMERG_PRECTOT (GPM IMERG) and PRECTOTCORR (MERRA-2 bias-corrected precipitation)

nfhl.dataset: National Flood Hazard Layer, Flood Hazard Zones (layer 28), queried at each point
nfhl.notes: The zone effective on the retrieval date, not the map in force in August 2017.

hwm.provider: U.S. Geological Survey (USGS), Short-Term Network (STN) Flood Event Data

fields.hFt: height of the mark above the ground at the mark, feet (null when not recorded or zero)
fields.elevFt: elevation of the mark, feet, in the datum given by vdatum
fields.quality: USGS quality class with its stated vertical uncertainty

hwm.notes: A high-water mark records how high water reached at one place. Marks were collected where crews went, mostly along rivers, bayous and the coast; the absence of a mark is not evidence that a place stayed dry.
